667: \begin{proposition}
668: \label{prop:hopf-identity-application}
669: Let $\nu\in \decomp_{\varphi}$ be tall with $\nu_B\neq \emptyset$.
670: Then
671: \[\mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}(\nu) =
672: (-1)^{|\nu_B|+1}(1\otimes \overline{s}_{(\nu_B)'}). \]
673: \end{proposition}
674: \begin{proof}
675: We proceed by induction on $N=|\nu_B|$. The base case is $|\nu_B|=1$. In this case, Algorithm~1 outputs $\xi^{(0)}=\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_1\otimes 1)$, so
676: \[\mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}(\nu)=\xi^{(0)}=\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_1\otimes 1) = \sum_{|\theta|=1} c_{(0),\theta}^{(1)} (1\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta}) = 1\otimes \overline{s}_1.\]
677: Suppose $|\nu_B|=k>1$. Construct the tensor $\xi^{(0)}$ from $\nu$, so
678: \begin{align*}
679: \xi^{(0)}&=\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\nu_B}\otimes 1)\\
680: &=\sum_{\lambda\subsetneq \nu_B}\sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq (n-r)^r\\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}} c_{\lambda,\theta}^{\nu_B} (\overline{s}_\lambda\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta}).
681: \end{align*}
682: Since there are finitely many nonzero terms occurring in the double sum, let us list them out explicitly as
683: \[
684: \xi^{(0)}= (1\otimes \overline{s}_{\nu_B})+\sum_{p=1}^L c_{\lambda^p,\theta^p}^{\nu_B}(\overline{s}_{\lambda^p}\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta^p}),
685: \]
686: where $1\leq |\lambda^p|<k$ for each $p$. Set $\varphi^{p} = (n,r,i,j,a,b,|\lambda^p|)$ for each $p$.
687: From Proposition \ref{clm:3}, it follows that $\mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}$ satisfies the ``depth-first search'' recurrence
688: \[\mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}(\nu) = (1\otimes \overline{s}_{\nu_B}) - \sum_{p=1}^L c_{\lambda^p,\theta^p}^{\nu_B} \mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}(i^j,\lambda^p)(1\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta^p}).\]
689: By the induction assumption,
690: \[\mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi^{p}}(i^j,\lambda^p)(1\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta^p}) = (-1)^{|\lambda^p|+1}(1\otimes \overline{s}_{(\lambda^p)'}\overline{s}_{\theta^p}) \text{ for each }1\leq p\leq L. \]
691: Thus,
692: \begin{align*}
693: \mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}(\nu) &= (1\otimes \overline{s}_{\nu_B}) + \sum_{p=1}^L c_{\lambda^p,\theta^p}^{\nu_B} (-1)^{|\lambda^p|}(1\otimes \overline{s}_{(\lambda^p)'}\overline{s}_{\theta^p})\\
694: &=(1\otimes \overline{s}_{\nu_B}) +\sum_{\substack{|\lambda|\geq 1\\ \lambda\subsetneq \nu_B}}\sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq (n-r)^r\\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}} c_{\lambda,\theta}^{\nu_B} (-1)^{|\lambda|}(1\otimes \overline{s}_{\lambda'}\overline{s}_{\theta})\\
695: &=\sum_{\lambda\subsetneq \nu_B}\sum_{\substack{\theta\subseteq (n-r)^r\\|\theta|=N-|\lambda|}} c_{\lambda,\theta}^{\nu_B} (-1)^{|\lambda|}(1\otimes \overline{s}_{\lambda'}\overline{s}_{\theta}).
696: \end{align*}
697: The lemma then follows if one can prove that
698: \[\sum_{\lambda,\theta}(-1)^{|\lambda|}c_{\lambda,\theta}^{\nu_B}\overline{s}_{\lambda'}\overline{s}_{\theta}=0.\]
699: In Lemma \ref{lem:hopf-identity} below, we prove an analogous identity holds in $\Lambda$.
700: Projecting from $\Lambda$ down to $\overline{\Lambda}$ via the (linear) quotient map $s_\lambda\mapsto \overline{s}_{\lambda}$ completes the proof.
701: \end{proof}
702: \begin{lemma}
703: \label{lem:hopf-identity}
704: For any partitions $\lambda,\mu$ and any partition $\nu\neq \emptyset$,
705: \[\sum_{\lambda,\mu}(-1)^{|\lambda|}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\nu}s_{\lambda'}s_{\mu}=0.\]
